content:
incident-bot: Pager: SEV2 - GPU cluster instability detected (multiple node resets). Pager link: https://pager.example/incident/1747000000 :rotating_light:

alice_oncall: I got the page - seeing elevated 5xx rates for hosted inference in us-west-2. Notifying infra.

ben_sre: I'm pulling logs. Early signs: repeated GPU driver resets and Xid errors on node gpu-03 and gpu-07. Containers restarting.

carol_runtime: Which models/queues are impacted? Any OOMs in the runtime?

alice_oncall: Most errors are on our v2-generation pods (gpt-mid). Latency spikes for streaming requests, about 10-20% errors.

ben_sre: Pasting relevant dmesg/nvidia output snippet:

```
[  123.456789] NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID=0, GPU has fallen off the bus
[  123.457001] kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, Graphics Exception
[  123.457210] nvidia: GPU 0: driver reset
[  124.001234] gpu-monitor: ECC error count increased on GPU 0: 14 -> 120
```

ben_sre: And container logs show repeated OOM/killed events and kubelet restarting the device plugin.

```
I0210 01:02:03.123456 1 nvidia-device-plugin.go:243] Device plugin reported unhealthy device: GPU-0
k8s_container: oom_kill: process "model-worker" cgroup memory+swap used 3.2G exceed
```

dan_infra_oncall: I'll cordon the affected nodes and drain them to stop new scheduling. Recommendation: avoid rolling all GPUs at once to keep capacity.

alice_oncall: Go ahead cordon gpu-03 and gpu-07. Use graceful drain with --ignore-daemonsets.

dan_infra_oncall: Running:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-03
kubectl drain gpu-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
kubectl cordon gpu-07
kubectl drain gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```

dan_infra_oncall: Drains started, moving pods to other healthy GPU nodes. Some pods are pending due to resource fragmentation.

carol_runtime: Driver resets indicate underlying GPU hardware or driver bug. Quick mitigation options: restart nvidia-driver daemonset on node, toggle ECC if that's safe for prod, or move workloads to reserved non-ECC pool.

ben_sre: I'm seeing persistent Xid 79/31 and ECC correctable error counters climbing. That usually means hardware flakiness (ECC faults) or a bad driver interaction under our load pattern.

erin_prod_ops: Customer impact: we have 4 active enterprise customers in us-west on dedicated capacity; their requests are getting 500s or long tails. Not yet full outage but degraded SLA. Informing CSMs.

alice_oncall: Ben, can you open an NVIDIA support case and attach dmesg + nvidia-smi -q output? Also collect GPU serials for the nodes.

ben_sre: Opening case now. Case #NVID-174700. Attaching logs. Quick commands I ran:
```
nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,DRIVER,CEC -i 0
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.errors.uncorrected.volatile,temperature.gpu --format=csv
```
Sample nvidia-smi excerpt:
```
==============NVSMI LOG==============
Memory ECC Mode : On
ECC errors (volatile): 120
ECC errors (aggregate): 358
Driver Version : 535.54.03
```

carol_runtime: Driver version noted. We recently rolled 535.54.03 last week. We could attempt to revert to 525.x stable that previous stacks used. Reverting requires node reboot and careful rollout.

alice_oncall: For immediate relief: keep nodes cordoned, restart nvidia-device-plugin daemonset on a healthy node hosting evicted pods to reattach devices. If pods still OOM after move, scale down batch size for models temporarily.

ben_sre: Performed device-plugin restart on node gpu-02 where some pods landed. Command used:
```
kubectl rollout restart ds nvidia-device-plugin -n kube-system
```
Some pods came back up healthy. Latency improved on those pods.

dan_infra_oncall: While we drain the two problematic nodes, I'm tagging them as hardware_unstable and creating a maintenance ticket for replacement with cloud provider.

carol_runtime: Note: a driver "soft-reset" can clear Xid transiently but if ECC counters keep increasing it's probable faulty memory or PCI bus. We'll treat soft reset as temporary.

ben_sre: We tried a driver reload on gpu-03 (`systemctl restart nvidia-docker`), it cleared Xid for ~10 minutes, then repeated.

alice_oncall: Escalation decision: escalate to oncall senior (carol) and engage vendor (NVIDIA/cloud infra). Ben please continue capture-trace logs.

ben_sre: Adding perf counters and ioctl traces. Also capturing full nv-host logs and `/var/log/messages` spans.

incident-bot: Update: Status -> mitigation in progress. Impacted customers notified via CSMs. Next update in 15m.

erin_prod_ops: Confirmed CSMs notified; some customers requested dedicated fallbacks. We're enabling fallback routing to our non-GPU (CPU) endpoints for the highest SLA customers. Doing a config flip for the 3 customers flagged.

alice_oncall: Good. That will reduce customer-visible errors while we work nodes.

carol_runtime: Plan for next 30-60 min: 1) keep gpu-03 & gpu-07 cordoned; 2) migrate critical traffic to cpu fallback for enterprise customers; 3) attempt controlled driver rollback on a single repro node (gpu-05) to validate; 4) if rollback stable, schedule a staged rollback across fleet with reboots; 5) if hardware confirmed, replace gpu-03/gpu-07 nodes.

ben_sre: Kicked off driver rollback test on gpu-05 to driver 525.85. Waiting for node reboot.

```
# example commands used for rollback
apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-525
reboot
```

ben_sre: Post-rollback quick check:
```
Driver Version : 525.85.12
ECC errors volatile: 0 (reset after reboot)
```
Initial post-rollback load test looks stable for 45m on gpu-05. No Xid observed.

alice_oncall: If test holds, proceed staged rollout overnight with 1 node at a time and monitor ECC/Xid counters for 1 hour each. Keep two hot spare nodes.

dan_infra_oncall: Cloud provider confirmed gpu-03 has anomalous ECC history and scheduled replacement. Provider ticket: CP-7892.

ben_sre: NVIDIA support replied: asked for full job traces and kernel-driver combos. They flagged known issues in 535 driver family under certain ECC patterns. Recommended rollback or firmware update.

erin_prod_ops: Notifying affected customers with mitigations and ETA for resolution ~4-6 hours.

alice_oncall: Handoff: my oncall ends in 30m. Ben, you take the overnight oncall and continue the staged rollout if test passes. I'll leave notes in postmortem draft channel.

ben_sre: Acknowledged. I'll keep watch and escalate to hardware if counters climb again. Ben -> taking handoff.

carol_runtime: I'll coordinate the staged rollback schedule with infra and set alerts to auto-stop rollout if Xid or ECC counters exceed threshold.

incident-bot: Update: Status -> partial mitigation. Two nodes cordoned, driver rollback test successful on one node, customer fallbacks enabled. Next update in 30m.

alice_oncall: Final note before handoff - collect these logs for postmortem: dmesg spans, nvidia-smi query history, pod evictions timestamps, routing flip records.

ben_sre: Copying artifacts to /mnt/incidents/1747000000/ and creating ticket for postmortem.

erin_prod_ops: CSMs updated; customers asked for post-incident RCA. We'll add timeline and mitigation steps.

carol_runtime: Action items assigned: ben_sre - continue monitoring + contact cloud/hw vendor; dan_infra_oncall - coordinate node replacement; erin_prod_ops - customer comms; alice_oncall - postmortem owner.

ben_sre: Last note: observed one uncorrectable ECC on gpu-07 -> suggests imminent replacement. Cloud provider already scheduled.

alice_oncall: Thanks team. Handoff complete. I'll file final incident record and schedule postmortem meeting tomorrow.

incident-bot: Incident timeline saved. Severity downgraded to SEV3 after mitigation.

(THREAD END)
